About the mystery of the Trinity

Beloved and respected, all our members who follow the orthodox education that we convey on John's Repentance website; today, we have sent you the following basic lesson based on the topic, so we entrust you all to read and learn from it.

Mystery

The basis and center of religious education is the acceptance of God. Next questions: Who is God? How his character revealed? Does it have a body? etc., are answered with the list of religious education; and this education is called a mystery because it is understood only by faith. So, mystery in this lesson mean spiritual, subtle, invisible, unknown, admirable and understood only by faith. Because either it is revealed by the extent of faith; but for those who do not believe, it is a hidden secret. Because, it cannot be reached through physical knowledge and scientific wisdom. Or, even if we say that we know and understand it, it is said that it is impossible to know the full extent of the mystery, except that we might   understand only to the extent that it is enough for the survival of the soul .

Trinity

Trinity is a noun derived from the Geez verb that means three. This is the lesson we learn about the trinity of God's body. Trinity is very different from three. For three speaks of three different things, and trinity speaks of three things in one thing. Therefore, when talking about trinity, it is necessary to talk about unity. 

Therefore, in the mystery of the Trinity, we learn not only about the threeness of God's body, but also about the unity of his character. In short, Trinity is the teaching that God is one and three. 

Their trinity is:- in name, in task, and in body.

Their unity is :- in character, in divinity, in power, in rulling, in will, in creating this world from non-existence to existence, as well as in feeding creation, protecting it, and in suspending this world.

Trinity means: Father has perfect form, perfect face, perfect body. And the Son has a perfect form, a perfect face and a perfect body. The Holy Spirit has a perfect form, a perfect face and a perfect body. The Father's body is always the Father's. The Son's body is always the Son's; The body of the Holy Spirit is always the Holy Spirit. That is, the bodies do not change, do not exchange, do not absorb. In their position, in their appearance and in their name, they will remain forever on their own. The names by which the bodies are called also remain unchanged for their bodies. Therefore, just as we say that the Trinity is three in body, so we say three in their name as well; and these Trinity Names are: Father, Son, Holy Spirit, (Matthew 28:19  ; Psalm 33:14, 118:73, Isaiah 66:1, Genesis 18:1-4 Matthew 3:16)  

(የግብር ሦስትነት ስንል፦ አብ ወላዲ አስራጺ ነው፤ ወልድ ተወላዲ ነው፤ መንፈስ ቅዱስ ሰራጺ ነው። )

Let's look at what the Bible says about the unity and trinity of the Mystery of the Trinity:

In the Old Testament

1.  "God said: let us make man in our image, after our likeness" (Genesis 1:26) Here: "God said" indicates unity, while "let us create man in our image" describes being more than one.

2.   "The Lord God said, Adam became as one of us to know good and evil" (Genesis 3:22). Here, "God said" refers to oneness, while "as one of us" refers to more than one.

3.  When God willed to create Eve, who will be his helper for Adam: “And the LORD God said, it is not good that the man should be alone; Let's create a suitable assistant for him” (Genesis 2:18). Here also, "God said" refers to oneness, while "Let’s create" refers to more than one.

4.  Another one, when the sons of Noah rebelled against God and started building a tower in the field of Sanatsor: "God said, Come, let us go down, as if they had lost their language there so that one would not hear the words of the other". Here, the word 'God said' indicates unity and the word 'let's go. down' indicates that there is more than one.

So, the verses we mentioned above are saying that God is one in character, divinity, creating and sustaining this world, and not one in body. However, they do not clearly explain that it is three, except that it is not physically one. However, when we continue reading the bible through, it is known that God is three in body. For example:-

5.  When God revealed himself to Abraham, "At noon, while he was sitting at the door of his tent, God appeared to him through the tree of Meri. He lifted up his eyes and saw three men standing before him. When he saw them, he ran from the door of the tent to meet them. He bowed to the earth. He said, "Lord, if I have found favor in your sight, I beg you not to let your servant pass over me." "And he lifted up his eyes and behold, he saw three men standing before him," and the saying that God is three in person (Trinity). And in the speech of Abraham, "O Lord, if I have found favor in your sight, I beseech you not to let your servant pass away from me." This indicates that God is one in character, will and power.

6.  In addition; When the prophet Isaiah explained the trinity, "I saw God sitting on a long and high throne, and the area of his garment filled the temple. ..And the seraphim were standing above him. And they were shouting to each other: "Holy, Holy, Holy, the Lord of hosts, the whole earth is full of his glory." The word refers to the unity and trinity of the Trinity. (Isaiah 6:3)

The New Testament

1.  The New Testament is an age of revelation. And it is God Himself who is revealed. The revelation that has been revealed in this age is very unique and clear compared to the revelation that was revealed to others in different ways previously. St. Paul explained this as follows: "Since ancient times, God has spoken to our fathers through prophets in many ways, and He has spoken to us at the end of this age through His Son, whom He made the heir of all things, and through whom He created the worlds." (Hebrews 1:1)

If a person falls into sin, how can it be difficult for him to repent? We should never feel overwhelmed or afraid. When a person is ashamed to talk about their sins, they run away from repentance, pile sin on top of sin, and keep the door wide open for more sin.

When a person commits a sin, they usually pretend that they have benefited and are happy, but later the results are not beneficial. This is a hindrance to repentance which is the method that is most commonly used by the devil to prolong the time for people to repent and to keep them in sin and to prevent them from revealing the secrets of sin that he practices secretly and the methods he used to make them captives of sin.

Among the ways of salvation that Satan fights against, there is nothing greater than repentance. Repentance destroys all the buildings of sin that the enemy, the devil, has built to destroy the lives of Christians. Repentance wipes out all sins - This is a great mystery that is performed by the grace of God. 

We are humiliated when we first commit the sin, and we are glorified when we say and confess the sin we have committed. By sinning, we were dirty, damaged, defiled, but when we repent, we are being sanctified, freed and glorified. 

The idea that our dear member raised is one which many people do either without knowing, without thinking it is bad, or knowingly, influenced by peers or by satanic entertainment industries. Later, they find it difficult to get out as easily as they entered it. Whichever it may be, by sinning, we lose God, by sinning, by sinning we live in darkness, and darkness is Sheol, eternal fire.

Our dear member stated, “I am ashamed to express the wrongs I have done to a confession father.”

But yet, repentance is to regret what we have done; it is saying that "I have done things that aren’t expected of a believer of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ." It is to say that we should accuse/judge ourselves before being accused by other people. It starts when a person accuses themselves, when they reveal their secrets to themselves, and when they are ashamed of what they have done in the past. It is followed by confessing our sins with heartfelt regrets before God. We should not be ashamed or embarrassed when we confess our sins as we were not ashamed or embarrassed when we were doing it because when we were doing the wrongdoings, we were dying but with confession, we are making reconciliation with God, and we are being saved. We are coming from death to life and coming out of darkness to light. It is a way that we are starting to live together with God. 

When we go to a confession father to repent for what we have done, we are admitting our hate for the sins and deciding that we would not do them again. St. Paul wrote, in 1 Corinthians 11: 31, “For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judges.” Repentance is when we, the sinners, judge ourselves and our sins. Therefore, what our questioner mentioned to us will be an answer for all of us, to say that we should be ashamed of our sins, repent, and decide not to do it again, but we should not be afraid to confess our sins to our fathers and repent.

Acts 3:19, St Paul wrote, “Repent therefore and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord.” 
Matthew 9:13 also mentions, “...For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners, ]to repentance.”  Therefore, it is the sinner who needs repentance. Our brothers and sisters, you must understand that no matter how serious our sins are, we must come to God in repentance, believing that we will be forgiven and that we will be cleansed. We have the opportunity to choose a confession father or a spiritual father who is a true guardian, mentor, and teacher. You are expected to state your repentance in detail without being ashamed or embarrassed by your sins to your spiritual father. As said in the book, the priest means the grave, because the grave does not reveal everything, and the priest does not speak about anyone's sin, he should be a secret keeper.

Just as water washes the cleanest and the dirtiest, without discrimination, so should the Priest wash away the sins of the child indiscriminately, and not speak of the sins he hears. Perhaps, if there is a Priest who speaks, he is responsible to God, not us. But since we are told to go and examine ourselves to the priest, it means that we should go and confess our sins to our repentance father. It is God who commanded us to confess our sins. It is written in Matthew chapter 8:4 "And Jesus said to him, “See that you tell no one; but go your way, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.” So, we advise our fellow members to do as it is told. If in case you don't have a father of repentance, no Christian should spend a day without a father of repentance. Having a father of repentance and repenting is a spiritual obligation. And so we advise you to look for a spiritual father, talk to the head priest of your parish, and consult with friends and family who have a father of repentance. How to overcome repeated sin and discouragement?

👉🏾Question: How does one overcome feelings of defeat and discouragement when falling into the same sin continually?
How to accept God's love and grace and not give up / lose hope with struggles that come with my journey with God? 
I tend to fall short of the goals I set for myself in spiritual life and the discouragement / feeling depressed about that holds me back from making progress. 

Thank you and May God bless your service! 

👉 Answer: This is a very important question because a lot of people confess their sins many times and go back to it many times. The main cause of this is not knowing what sin is and not understanding the depths of it's consequences. 

If a person confess their sins without understand what sin is, they will most likely fall back into it. If a person confesses their sins without understanding the benefits of repentance, it will be very hard for them to come back to repentance.

Hence we first need to learn about sin, it's consequences and the benefits of repentance. We need to learn from people that have fallen into sin, we need to know that sin separates us from God, sin deprives us from peace, sin brings curses to our lives, sin is the worst thing one can do. 

People who have fallen into sin have lost God, lost blessings, lost peace, lost life and can't even get alone with themselves. That is why Adam and Eve had a hard time living together after they fell into sin. Adam had asked Eve to get away from him, to depart form him accusing her to be the reason of his fall. People who have fallen into sin can't live with others nor be comfortable in their own skin. That is why Judas of Iscariot, who sold our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ with $30 thought that he was doing good for himself, that he would live but he couldn't. He threw away the money, hanged himself up on a tree and died after suffering for 40 days. Hence we need to understand that people trapped in sin can't live with God, with others nor with themselves. This, we have to believe before confessing. 

One needs to understand the depths of sin's consequences, and also understand the benefits of repentance. We need to learn from people who changed their lives and were healed through repentance. It is only then that we will have not repeatedly fall back to sin. 

We need to believe that everything is possible with God and nothing without Him. On Matthew 21:21, our Lord tells us "if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but also if you say to this mountain, ‘Be removed and be cast into the sea,’ it will be done." Hence why do we give up? We are winners in Christ, we fall and we get back up but we should never give up, why do we give up? Are we not the ones He created in His own image? Are we not the ones whom He appointed as rulers over creatures? It is us that He has delivered from the bondage of the devil by becoming one of us, it is for us that He has given his Holy Blood and Holy Flesh. It is for us that is given the interception of the apostles, the prophets, the angels, the saints, the virgins, the monks, our Lady Virgin Mary and others. Hence how can we give up? It is for us that our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ established the mystery of Repentance so we can be reconciled with Him if we fall. Hence we do not give up. The holy water, the cross, the priests, the gospel, the prayer books, the advisors, the teachers, the fasts, prostration and countless more are ours. Hence how can we give up? We don't!

The biggest and most gravious temptation of the devil is to make us give up. But we Christians never give up. Let us recall a story of a monk: There was a father who repeatedly sinned and repeatedly confessed. Then the devil said to him: "Are you not ashamed? Everyday you sin and everyday you confess it, you go to your spiritual father and confess the sin knowing you will fall tomorrow as well." Then this father said to him: "You that have no repentance, you that do not wish to be reconciled with God, you be ashamed but how can I be ashamed since repentance was established for me". Truly, repentance was established for us so we shouldn't give up.

The devil makes sin seem trivial for those who haven't previously fallen into it by showing them people who have fallen into sin and saying: "what consequences did they have to face for their sins? Your sins are nothing compared to their sins, you have not done anything wrong" Then he teaches us to sin step by step making us immune and ignorant to the consequences of it.

Then once we have fallen deep into it, he says: "Look at you, do you think God is going to forgive you? Are you not ashamed to approach God with all these sins? Are you not ashamed to go to a prist and admit to all these sins? You shameful being!" To make us think that God doesn't forgive, painting him as cruel. 

Hence we should understand that this is the devil's trap and get up when we fall, never give up. We have the hope to inherit our Lord's Kingdom, which is eternal and absolute. Hence how can we give up? We don't! God died for us, it is for us that he gave his Holy Blood and his Holy Flesh, it is for us that he gave his mother the Virgin Mary. Hence we don't give up. 

May God help us confess all our sins and live a life or repentance so we can stay in His house until the last breathe and inherit His Kingdom.

👉🏾 Question: I, as an Orthodox believe that Jesus Christ is God. There are also Bible verses that prove this. Therefore, how can we explain to those who do not believe in simple language? Becauseb this is difficult to understand it.

Answer: The question is related to theology and the mystery of the Trinity. He said not only 'my father', but 'he has begotten me'. To understand this, it is necessary to know about the mystical Trinity and the mystical incarnation. Previously, when we talked about the divinity of Jesus Christ, we talked extensively about the names of God. There are names by which the Lord was called in ancient times, that were unknown before His birth. And Jesus is his New Testament name. The names we call 'Jesus Christ', 'Jesus' are when he became flesh, became a perfect God (he was already God), a perfect Man; He is a Man and is God. He is God even after he dies, rises, and ascends. Therefore, when he becomes a man, what we speak about him, what He too speaks is that he speaks as if there is another father, another superior authority, to mean for the united body; The flesh that was a creature is saying that I have become God. (because he  was God before He united the flesh;   the flesh became absolute God when   Divinity united it; and He became absolute Man, absolute God) Jesus is the son of man and the son of God.

Our Lord Jesus is one of the Trinity Body, who was and is Glorified, praised equally together with the Almighty father & Holy spirit, before the creation of the world and forever. so, God the Son is God in a different form, he is the creator, he is almighty, he is pure and he is holy. When he was born from the virgin Mary, there is a body that arose from her, and he chose her as a pure saint for motherhood, starting from the womb, so that the sin of Adam would not be passed on to her. This is the teaching of our church, and this is what our holy fathers have revealed to them and said about her in all their books and common teachings.

In the holy book, when St. Gabriel announces her purity, virginity and is different from all women; he does not describe her femininity in the language used by other people. For example, a girl is called a 'woman' after losing her virginity; but  our Lady Virgin Mary is a virgin forever. She is a virgin before her conception, during her conception, and after her conception. She is a virgin before, during, and after giving birth.

Therefore, the flesh united from this mother is perfect God. What happened to the flesh that was the creature? He became a god. This is why:

1.  The expression "my father" refers to the birth of the pre-world without a mother. This is an inscrutable birth, it is a subtle birth, it is a birth beyond our imagination. Even we, let alone him, talk normally about the secret of reproduction from our mother and father,  but this even itself is abstract. Doctors confirm that a fetus lives in the mother's womb for nine months and five days before birth, and we know this from experience. But the secret of being born as a human being after this water and blood, as a boy or a girl, when he stayed in the mother's womb for 9 months and 5 days, what kind of food he was being fed, what kind of care, what kind of air he was getting, how he was born as a human being is amazing. After that, when we see how he comes from the darkness to the light world, from non-existence to existence, from the narrow to the wide world, this birth is a mystery. Hence, let alone the birth of God and the birth of man is even a subtle mystery.

The Meaning of Worthiness

Orthodox Faith: The person who approaches the Eucharist must be an Orthodox Christian having no doubt concerning the bread & wine being the true body and precious blood of Lord Jesus Christ.

Repentance & Confession: The person must be practicing the Sacrament of Repentance and Confession on regular basis as St. Paul said, “let a man examine himself” (1 Cor 11:28)

Reconciliation With Others: Lord Jesus Christ said, “If you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come offer your gift” (Mt 5:23-24)

True Worthiness is Feeling Unworthy: St. Paul, the meek and humble apostle said, “I know nothing against myself, yet I am not justified by this” (1 Cor 4:4)

Obeying The Church Rules: concerning food abstinence before communion, physical cleanliness, and early attendance of the liturgy.

👉 The Eucharist as a Sacrifice

The Orthodox Church believes and confesses that the Eucharist is a sacrifice and an offering to God in addition to being a Sacrament. The following supports this belief:

The words of Lord Jesus Christ Himself, “This is My blood of the new covenant, which is shed for many” (Mt 26:28; Mk 14:24) – “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is shed for you” (Lk 22:20) – “This is My body which is broken for you” (1 Cor 11:24) – “This is My body which is given for you” (Lk 22:19). Undoubtedly, the terms “broken body” and “shed blood” refer to a sacrifice.

The presence of an altar in the Church confirms that the Eucharist is a sacrifice. St. Paul said, “We have an altar from which those who serve the tabernacle (Jews) have no right to eat” (Heb 13:10). Isaiah the Prophet said, “In that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt” (Is 19:19), this is a specific prophecy about the Coptic (Egyptian) Church which proves the presence of altars in the Christian era and consequently the presence of a sacrifice (the Eucharist).

Malachi the Prophet prophesied about the New Testament offering saying, “I have no pleasure in you, says the Lord of hosts, nor will I accept an offering from your hands. For from the rising of the sun even to its going down, My name shall be great among the Gentiles; In every place incense shall be offered to My name, and a pure offering; For My name shall be great among the nations, says the Lord of hosts” (Mal 1:10-11). This “pure offering” is nothing but the Eucharistic offering that Christians offer on their altars, for at which point in history did the Gentiles “in every place” offer an offering to the Lord?

St. Paul said, “Observe Israel after the flesh: Are not those who eat of the sacrifices partakers of the altar? What am I saying then? That an idol is anything, or what is offered to idol is anything (else)? Rather, that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I do not want you to have fellowship with demons. You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you cannot partake of the Lord’s table and the table of demons” (1 Cor 10:18-21). The apostle is comparing the table (altar) of the Lord to the altar of the pagans upon which unacceptable demonic sacrifices were offered, which proves that the Eucharist that is offered on the Christian altar is indeed a sacrifice.

Source: ‘The Church Sacraments’ by Archdeacon Habib Guirgess.

Our body: If we lose  food for a few days or even for few hours for some people, it is definitely not possible to stay alive. This is one of the common weaknesses of the body where we lose our fleshly existence. Likewise, if the soul loses Christ's holy flesh and precious blood, it dies and has no life. It means that we have killed it. Therefore, in order to eat this eternal life, to drink that gives eternal life, we should learn what kind of system and what kind of spiritual preparation we should follow. We are commanded by God to live a Christian life, of which the Holy Eucharist is the foundation. Any teaching that keeps us away by threatening and exaggerating for other reasons is false teaching and should be avoided. 

Apostle St. Paul said that if we eat and drink the ultimate food of the soul without preparation and understanding, it will be a debt to us. This means that it is necessary to always have a life prepared for repentance and to accept those who are counselors in the affairs of our souls, the fathers of the church whom God has appointed as our servants and shepherds. In other words, we are commanded to always receive with repentance, so that we do not make this mistake that St. Paul wrote about (so that we do not receive without deserving or understanding this), but there is no occasion where we are commanded to depart from this mystery, not even for a single day.

Therefore, for those who are said to be before marriage, as we mentioned above, we should realize that we should continue to accept what we received in our childhood, that started from the time of Christianity,  until the end of our lives. But we should do this without committing any shame or sin as that is the only thing which keeps us away from the Holy Communion. Everyone knows what sin or shame is that keeps us away from the Holy Communion, even a child knows. There is no one who does not know the type of sin from the smallest to the highest level of sin. Murder, adultery, adultery, all these seeming sins can keep you away from the sacrament. But through repentant and reprimanded, you can continue the communion by repenting and being mentored and taught by their penitent father. 

Back to the question, it is to say that we should do this throughout our life, and it is not a matter of martial status. Both the male and female start participating in this sacrement at the time of their baptism and actively participate alone until they reach maturity age. After that, the man chooses someone who resembles him in his spiritual life and the woman chooses someone who resembles her in her spiritual life and they get married and continue with the Holy Communion together. Even those who are not married in the Holy Communion, without having this opportunity, come to repentance and they, too, can continue their holy purpose that they have abandoned. Because the Church has made a system for us, it has reconciliation for all from her creator.

To be continued 👇

(Continued part)👆👇.
 
In general, the sacrament does not depend on the state of marriage; After all, the Holy Church has never commanded us to stay away from the Holy Communion for a single day until marriage. This is an attitude that some people have brought by habit, or even counselors and teachers have been absorbed in the people's system, not God's system; and we need to understand that it is not the correct teaching of the Church. Besides, it is not an honor for us to continue to be a father of repentance for people living far from the Holy Communion, but a great shame. Why? The first and foremost task of a penitent father is to teach his penitent children, equip them for penance and Holy Communion, and watch over them to live steadfastly in this spiritual life. But as we can see what is happening in practice, does everyone who is a Christian receive the Holy flesh and the precious blood of Christ?  Not really.
 
On the other hand although it is not comparable with our faith, when we see other faith institutions around the world who claim to be in Christianity, even those who do not believe in partaking fekm His holy flesh and precious blood do not leave without receiving 'in rememberence' each time they come to their church, never. Our church, however, does not consider the Holy Communion as a memorial, and not do not take this mystery simply or boldly. Rather, we receive it believing that it is the real holy flesh and his noble blood that our Creator shed for us through all that suffering on Friday; and we accept it in the fear of God . This is Christian ethics. As Christian ethics, we correct our wrongdoing and accept it through a life of repentance. So, the only thing that may keeps us far from the Holy Communion before and during marriage is our own sin.

So the answer to the question is that if there is a time when we are different from Holy Communion, the biggest thing is our own reason. Thi may be, either we didn't get real lesson of the Orthodox Church; Or that we are not willing to repent for what we committed a sin; Or that we have not decided to stop that sin. But, in general, there is no time to deprive us the Holy Communion except in this way.

1.3. When we pray, we should face east. The east is always the manifestation of the Lord, and all good things emerge from the east like the rising sun. With spiritual justice, it has been decided that we should turn our faces to the east. The Holy Book tells us that God will come from the east in the last days to gather this world and call us in the resurrection, so we should turn to the east and pray.

1.4. When we begin to pray, we should make the sign of the cross on our whole body using our fingers. Before we begin to pray, we cover our faces and our whole bodies with the sign of the cross. This is to put the evil spirit that opposes us in our thoughts and challenges us not to connect with our Creator in prayer, with the power of the cross, to throw it under our feet or to keep it away from us altogether. When we make the sign of the cross, we should start from top to bottom, then from left to right. This is so that the thoughts of darkness can be pushed away from us, and we can walk in the light. We stretch out our index finger and make a cross by folding our middle finger and others and touch our face and our whole body from top to bottom and from left to right. When we pray, we say "Father" on the forehead, "Son" on the chest (heart), "Holy Spirit" on the left shoulder, "One God" on the right shoulder, and invoke the name of the Trinity.

"But if I cast out demons with the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come to you" (Luke 11:20), because the finger is a manifestation of God's power. Clergy fathers pray with the cross they hold, while lay people should pray by joining the fingers next to the thumb in the shape of a cross as described above. The spiritual secret behind this is as follows:

"In the name of the Father" means that God the Son, Jesus Christ, is the perfect God who was sanctified in heaven together with the Holy Spirit before the world.

Touching the heart with the word "Son" means that "Son" came down from heaven in a different body and took flesh from the body of the Holy Virgin Mary and soul from her soul and was conceived in a perfect union.

Writing from left to right, "The Holy Spirit, the One God" means that the Son of God, Jesus Christ, nailed His hands and feet with nails for us on Friday, and in His resurrection, from left to right, from hell to heaven, from suffering to peace, from death to life, from darkness to light, from sorrow to joy, to testify.

From top to bottom, from left to right, we mean a cross because it is the shape of a cross. Christ saved the world by hanging on the cross. The right is like heaven, and the left is an example of hell. (Article 14 of Justice King)

The times when we make the sign of the cross are as follows:
 
- When we want to pray,
- When we come to a word stated about the cross in the prayer 
– on the foods we eat and drink,
– On the clothes we wear,
– When we sleep; & when we wake up,
-  Before we start any spiritual and physical work, we should make a sign using our finger of the cross in a way discribed above.
 
1.5. We should pray with our eyes fixed on heaven. Question: God promised Adam that He would come and save him in five and a half days or 5500 years. How do we count the days of the week?
 
✍️Answer:- The Church has always taught that in order to save Adam and his descendants, God promised to be born as a man and save them. This promise was given to Adam when he fell into sin and asked for forgiveness. God promised him that He would be born of his son, be crucified, die, rise and save him. The period from the time Adam fell or when the promise was given until the day of our Lord's birth is known as "five and a half days", according to the Lord's words and revealed to the Scholars by the Holy Spirit.

The scholars, enlightened by the spirit of God, understood that "five and a half days in God's will is five thousand and five hundred years". This means that God's five days are equivalent to five thousand years and five years and six months in man's time. It is important to note that the apostle Saint Peter explained that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.

Therefore, the difference between God's calendar and our calendar is clear. What is counted as one day or one year by God is counted as a thousand to us. Thus, the seven days of one week period should be understood with the grace and spiritual permission given to us. We should consider what God's thoughts and calculations look like and understand that the time calculation in the Bible, as given by our ancestors, is five thousand and five hundred years, which is called "five and a half days" by the Lord.

Saint Paul has explained that the day of the Lord or the coming of the Lord is sudden and unexpected. Therefore, we must always be ready and live our lives in accordance with God's will.

This is a powerful message that was given on Mount Olivet, as the Church teaches about the last days and the second coming, which is the foundation of this concept.

So, how are these seven days calculated? We use the grace and the gift of the Holy Spirit to reflect on what we have and count the seven days and the years according to our beliefs. As a religion, we calculate time differently from the world, and we are now entering the eighth millennium based on our calculations.

Although we have the Bible, there is a difference between our calculation and God's formula, as His calculation is counted in thousands. According to our calendar, since the creation of the world, it has been 8,800 years until the birth of the Lord, which was 5,500 years, and after His birth, according to our calendar, it has been around 2,000 years.

We acknowledge that our calculation is different from God's kindness and calculation of time, as His idea of time is different from ours. We should accept it with grace and without interfering in God's plans or doubting His wisdom, even if our time seems long.

We believe that we have addressed the meaning of your question in the context that we understand, and we entrust you in the name of God to share this explanation with everyone as it will benefit all our families.

About #repentance #confession 

👉🏾 Question: How do I prepare to confess sin? 
 
Respected members who follow the Orthodox education and spiritual services on John's Repentance page, today we send an important lesson on repentance so we urge you to read and learn from it.
 
✍Answer: First of all, it is a pleasure to hear that you are preparing for repentance. This is an act of loyalty expected from a true Christian and is more sacred than anything else, so we entrust you to repent by standing firm in your aim until the end, and we declare that we are by your side with the spiritual service that we can help you in all your ways. Please note that we confirm our word by starting to send you important teaching and advice based on your questions, which explains the meaning and process of repentance below.
 
Because God is a God of love, he always waits for us to return with open arms and call him my children. When the prophet Ezekiel said that God does not like the death of a person and he likes the return of a person to repentance, ''Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin. Cast away from you all your transgressions, whereby you have transgressed; and make you a new heart and a new spirit: for why will ye die,...For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith the Lord GOD: wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye." (Ezekiel 18 30-32).
 
Before we come to the question that our dear member asked about how to repent, let us ask 'what is sin?' What is repentance?' Since we have to understand clearly, it is appropriate to put their meaning first as follows.
 
- Sin :- Sin is the loss of meaning, and its secret meaning is rebellion, wrongdoing, humiliation, falling, losing and stealing what we had, lack of honor, doing evil, breaking the law, falling away from the glory of heaven, doubting, submitting oneself to the work of destruction, collaborating with death, etc. Sin can make us think of all these details of failure.
 
- Repentance :- Repentance is the meaning and explanation of the word, sorrow, regret, anger, punishment, acceptance of the canon, paying compensation for the sin committed, believing in the wrongdoing and destruction. In addition, it is a final decision to not commit sins that would otherwise disobey the Creator and deprive him of heavenly eternal life.
 
The following are the important emotional and practical processes that a person who is ready to repent should acquire before repenting, i.e. the spiritual education or understanding that is called pre-repentance.
 
Repentance preparation procedures that help us understand repentance in the right way
 
- Repentance with real feelings: Before repenting, we must admit our own sinfulness and feel remorse.
This type of regret follows failure, embarrassment, shame, loss, mistakes. A person who knows his sinfulness, thinks about breaking the law, wronging God, other people, and his own soul, condemns himself with anger and sorrow, and regrets, and hates the sin he has committed. The burning of such a feeling in us is one of the signs that we are not sleeping comfortably in the bed of sin (it indicates that there is a sign of hope or regret left in us to repent). As the prophet advised us, "If you repent and cry, you will be saved" (Isaiah 30:15). Crying for the sins you have committed is a great and bright way to be saved and to find forgiveness for your sins.
 
- Hating sin: One of the behaviors that help us easily hate sin is fearing God. The wise Solomon said, "He who fears God hates sin; "He hates envy and pride, and hates evil ways" (Proverbs 8:13). He told us that if we do not hate the sin that we are often tempted by, it means that we have appointed the work of sin as a queen over ourselves.
846:
How do I prepare to confess sin?

(Part 2)

The great holy father, Mar Isaac, told us the great spiritual truth, "If the human being is not the enemy of sin first, he cannot take down sin from his head." Abhorrence is the greatest level of hatred, so it is necessary not only to abhor the practice of sin, but also to abhor the thought of that sin.

To repent of sin is to be ashamed of sin, to hate sin, and to turn back. A person who is ready to repent without a thorough understanding of these is not free from the slavery of sin, so he will not hesitate to return to his previous duty easily. Therefore, the first and most important thing that helps us start away from sin is to admit that we have sinned and confess to ourselves, and to hate sin. Hating sin is the greatest force that helps us separate from sin and leave it forever. We cannot truly repent of sinfulness while in love with sin, nor can we live with a problem that can be corrected and not be corrected without separating from it.
 
- Bringing a change in thinking: To solve a problem in any area of our life, we must have a different perspective and need from the previous one. Glory cannot be found in a lazy mind, problems cannot be solved by a needy (problem-creating) mind, it is impossible to love with a hateful mind, and it is difficult to hate with a loving heart. Nor will he come to repentance with a sinful mind. Therefore, any change requires a change of thinking first. For this, our greatest powers are faith, good vision, and hope. In this way, a sinner must first stop his sin and change from loving sin to hating his sin in order to repent spiritually. Because in a life of sin, we cannot understand the importance of righteousness.

- Not to worry, but to repent: A sinner who worries and a sinner who repents are completely different. Anxiety is a disorder of terror caused by the abundance and evil of our sinfulness, and this kind of temporary regret can occur even in a conscience that has not awakened from sin. But spiritual repentance comes next to knowing sinfulness, hating sin, and being ashamed of sin, and it is the first step of repentance. Saint Paul said in his second letter, "I am very glad that you are sorry for the sake of God, so that not even one of you may perish." Grief for God is repentance that gives eternal life" (2 Cor 7:9) "Return to me with all your heart, but do not tear your clothes, but your heart" (Job 2:13, Ps 50:17, Job 2:1)
 
- Using our free will for good deeds: Sin's greatest strength and confidence (guaranty) in us is our love for her, not her power. The devil has no other confidence without our consent. If we deny our will, if we overcome it, we will be rewarded. But if we give our consent to the work he offers us, we will be defeated and humiliated. If we remain losers, our defeat will not be inevitable for the time being. Because if Satan finds the small hole of will, he will lick it like a snake and widen it, and he will lose us from our God. When our evil will screams, it repeatedly whips us with the whip of sin and drives us down to the valley of death, hell, to the world of damnation, and store us there forever.
 
God predestined all human beings for life and salvation. But the decision is made when our free will is added to it. So whoever wants life can be saved. Salvation is in our hands. Our God always stretches out His hand and calls us to repentance so that we can use our free will to adjust and return to freedom. He who repents will be saved. He who refuses and ignores the call will perish.


May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always. 

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.

848:
How do I prepare to confess sin?

(Part 3)


Therefore, to briefly summarize the main tasks expected of a Christian who wants to repent:
 
1. First of all, he admits that he has committed a sin and repents to his conscience  and hates the sin.
 
2. Repenting about the sin or wrongdoing committed, confessing the wrongdoing to the Creator, God, in the morning and night with prayers and supplications and confessing the sin before God (Ps 50, Dan 9:5, Neh 1:6-7).

3. By forgiving all those who have wronged us, we break down the wall of enmity and win with love and live in peace with a perfect conscience for the sake of eternal life.
 
4. To talk about the wrongdoings and sins that we have done without hiding anything, to keep it in our mind in detail, and if we think that we will forget, to be prepared with a note.
 
5. Confession of sins to the priest (repentance). Since the priest is God's servant and is appointed over us for the sake of our souls, repenting by confessing our sins to the priest; It means repenting and confessing before God so that our sins can be forgiven. (Joshua 7:19 Matthew 3:6 Leviticus 5:5-6 Acts 19:18)
 
After we have repented, we must strive to continue our penitent life in the right way of righteousness:
 
- Doing righteous deeds: When the scholars of the church teach, they tell us that God does not like us to sit with our legs stretched out and say that it is always from Him to do it. He does not allow us to say that he gives us value without work. But first we should do our part and ask him to do his part for us. Therefore, it is very important to believe that our own decision has a very significant role in the security of the world and to implement it, which includes worshiping God, fasting, prayer, prostration, almsgiving and tithing. Absence of righteousness is the source of sin against us when our inner relationship with God begins to break down. At this time, sin easily rules over us. Therefore, if we know the root causes of our trials in advance, we should avoid them and protect ourselves and walk in a righteous way.
 
- Hating sin not only with knowledge, but also with will and emotion: Many people hate sin; we don't want to do it. But when our will exceeds our knowledge, we commit it again and again while knowing that it is the sin we hate. Therefore, we should hate sin not only with knowledge or fear, but also with will and emotion. Otherwise, if we hate it only because we know it is evil or because we believe in the judgment it will bring upon us, we will be hating it and obeying it because our will is with the flesh. Even if we say that we will fight for it, we will lose and fall because our fight is not from our feelings. When we are tempted by a bad habit, if the will (emotion) is not awakened to understand the extent of the sin, it is not possible to leave the sin, because it is not possible to say that I hate the sin. Saint Paul the Apostle said, "What I hate, I will also do" (Romans 7:19). Knowing all that is good, one of the problems in which we fall into sin due to the carnal will driven by passion is not applying knowledge and not aligning our knowledge with our feelings. In general, when we say that we hate sin, the hatred must be sincere and complete, that is, with will (emotion), knowledge, and with all our strength. This is possible by fulfilling God's commandment against sin word by word, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength" (Exodus 6:3).
849:
How do I prepare to confess sin?

(Part 4)

- Refraining from talking about sin and mocking it: Also, if we pretend to hate sin, but make fun of it, it means we don't hate it. "In the words of a sinful person, sin accumulates" (Sira 27:4) and "there is much sin in him, so do not let anything that is impure come out of your tongue" (Sira 23:13).

Therefore, even if we meet her (sin) again, ready and prepared as much as she wants, without arguing with ourselves, if our heart's will and our mind's knowledge work together as one and understand her futility, then it is known that our rejection of sin is perfect. It will be confirmed that we have identified her as our enemy. It is only a dog that returns to its vomit.
 
- Regularly read from spiritual things, and consult spiritual fathers: To avoid falling back into sin, regularly consult a penitent father or religious teacher, pray as much as possible, go to church and listen to the word of God, read spiritual books even at home, listen to spiritual teachings and hymns. It is important.

To sum up, we will now summarise to you what a Christian should do after washing his sinful body, since his whole life is clean and the way is straight for any spiritual service:

1. Above all, be careful not to return to sin again and defile your sacred life.

2 / Receiving Holy Communion, fasting, praying, and prostrating as much as you can without stopping and without tiring.

3/ Contributing what is due to the poor as uou can; and also to God (tithe) 10% from what you earn.

4/ Regularly receiving advice and obedience from fathers, coming to church in the daily/weekly program, learning the word of God, sanctifying.

5/. Always read spiritual books that serve as a close teacher and mentor, and more than that, do your part to live in peace and love with patience and wisdom in your life, workplace, social affairs with all mankind.

Since it is possible to do all these and other spiritual things as a whole when a person's life is renewed through repentance, may God help you to put into practice the spiritual advice given to you above, believing that God will keep your life clean and holy.

About #fasting 

👉🏾 Question፦ Should you accept something offered to you during great fasting that is not permitted or at a time before you should break your fast? On work or in a family gathering with others who are not fasting?

 What happens if you eat something that was offered that contains meat... without knowing....but prayed and made the sign of the cross before eating...What should you do after finding out?

Answer፦ Whether it is at work or with people who are not fasting, if someone offers something that is not permitted during fasting before the end of the fasting period, one should not accept it. It is important to understand that fasting is mandatory for Orthodox Christians. There is no excuse for not fasting, the only exception would be health conditions or special circumstances like our sisters who live in Arab countries working as mades in a house where there is no option to fast. The Church has seven fasting periods and every Orthodox Christian is obligated to fast during these seven fasts. The start of these fasts is announced in all churches, on social media Orthodox services, and we hear about them from friends and family. Thus, one should fast after hearing all of this.

It is inconvenient to fast for those that don't live in a Christian county. If one lives in a Christian country, they must fast during the seven fasting periods. It is not right to eat anything during fasting. However, if he/she is sick and lives in an Islamic country, such as an Arab country, where food with meat and butter are common, and it is difficult to find clean bread, eating during fasting may be allowed for a specific reason like this. However one must communicate this with their father of pennance before deciding for themselves. 

If one decides to eat diary food during fasting periods, the Church cannot force him to fast but he can fast when he is willing to obey the Church's commandments and fast. For example, when Adam was told not to do something, it was prescribed because it would harm him. He knew not to eat from the tree of knowledge which is why he was able to enjoy 7 years of peace and unity with God in Heaven. Similarly, if a person is told not to eat poison, he knows that it will harm him, so he will not eat it. Therefore, eating what is said not to eat during fasting is like drinking poison. Adam lived peacefully for about seven years without eating what he was told not to eat. But after eating, the God-like Lord lost his place in heaven and became a wandering refugee. This happened because he ate what he was told not to eat and did what he was told not to do. It means that if a person does what he is told not to do, he will get hurt. We should all know this. But if there is something beyond our control, God knows everything, God is merciful and cares for us more than we do. If we can fast and choose not to do so, we will be asked for this, just like Adam was held accountable. When the devil asked him to eat, he could have said that he would not eat, but he willingly ate. 

If someone unknowingly eats something not permitted during fasting, they should tell their repentant father, and it's not something they did knowingly. They should not break or interrupt their fast. They should continue to fast and tell their father of pennance about the problem they faced. Therefore, for repentance, they should approach their father and accept the canon. If we accidentally fail while doing spiritual work, we should be careful not to fail again. 

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every language that He has created, today and always.

I was molested by a priest when I was young, I now doubt the truthfulness of the #Church, what do you advice me? 

👉Question: Hello, 

I was once molested by a priest when I was around 17 years old. At that time I didn't process it because it was a traumatic event. As an adult now, I look back and I have a hard time trusting people in church. I know that there is a difference between the Holy church and the people within.I know that God and his church is true and perfect and that the people that attend the church are imperfect and sinners. However, it's sad that the place that people go to for peace can have people that can be evil in it. I know that the devil is also at work here but If we can't be safe in church, where else are we supposed to be safe? 

I also sometimes wonder how people in church, especially a church leader like a priest, do such a thing. One of the doubts that I have and my question is : Is church a place that's used to manipulate people for their own benefits? Does God even exist or is the church a system that is set up for using people? I know that this is just a doubt and that God is Holy and perfect and that it's an issue of the people in the church but I do wonder about this sometimes and it creates a doubt.  

Thank you, 

Answer: The word Church has three meanings. The first is a building, which is a church, where the word of God is preached, Christ's holy body and precious blood is served, where believes participate in the different mysteries of Christianity and where they perform their worship. This is called the Church.

The second is the union of believers, the congregation, which is also called the church. This becomes very clear in Matthew chapter 18, verses 15-20, where it says: "Moreover if your brother sins against you, go and tell him his fault between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother. But if he will not hear, take with you one or two more, that ‘by the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.’ And if he refuses to hear them, tell it to the church. But if he refuses even to hear the church, let him be to you like a heathen and a tax collector." When it says "to the church," it does not mean the building or the stone, but the assembly, the believers, the union who gather in the church and praise God. So, the union of believers is called the congregation church. This union includes holy angels, holy people, and Christ as the head of the church. Those who are alive on earth, those who are in heaven, those who are in the hidden world with God, and where the Virgin Mary is, are all part of the Church.

From the two definitions above, it is incorrect to say that the Church is wrong; an individual who is a member of the Church may or may not be wrong. When we say the Church, we mean the one founded by God, including those who have finished their struggle, those who have not finished, the monastic fathers who are hidden, Saint Michael, Saint Gabriel, and the Virgin Mary. The Church is a united union, and while a deacon can make a mistake, we need to recognize this.

According to Orthodox teaching, the Church does not teach that even a bishop cannot make mistakes. Until he finishes his struggle, the bishop, monk, and priest may or may not make mistakes, but the Church never makes mistakes. The individual and the Church are not the same. They are separate. Doubt arises when we link the individual and the Church together. If we all think that way, we are mistaken.

Thirdly, Every believer who is baptized and receives Christ's holy body, which is the dwelling place of Christ, is called a church. As 1 Corinthians chapter 3 verse 16 states: "Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?" However, every believer, every individual, or Orthodox believer can be God's abode without separating from the community. If he is separated from the community, he cannot be God's abode and hence can't be called a church.

(Continues)👇🏾

For example, the devil, who was created as the archangel, made a mistake. But the other angels didn't follow him because they know the Church is right. The wrong devil mislead Adam but all of Adam's children didn't follow Adam's path thinking that Adam was right. Adam realized his mistake and returned.

In the same way, the people of Noah's time were wrong, and Noah did not follow them thinking they were right. He opposed their ideas. The people of Lot's time were also wrong, and Lot did not say to those who were wrong, "You are right." Our fathers knew that individuals make mistakes, so they stayed where they were, and God continued to speak to them. Judas, one of the twelve apostles chosen after Christ became a man, made a mistake, and the apostles at that time did not say that Judas was right. Instead, they condemned his actions. The sons of the priest Eli were doing abominable things. One of these acts was to sleep with women in the holy place. These were the priests, and they were blaspheming. Even though the priests made mistakes, the Church itself was not wrong. God punished them for their sins, and caused the Ark to be captured by Zion, Eli and his sons to die in the same day. This highlights the fact that even though individuals within the Church may make mistakes, the Church itself is founded on the teachings of Christ and is therefore incapable of making mistakes.

In summary, while individuals may make mistakes and fall short of the values upheld by the Church, it is important to distinguish between the actions of individuals and the Church as an institution. The Church is founded on the word of God and the teachings of Christ, and is therefore incapable of making mistakes.

Question: I can't get my husband to go to church and even if he does, he wants to leave early. I have boys, what should I do?

✍️Answer: - Dear member, it would have been helpful if you listed the reasons why your husband does not go to church. A Habit is valuable when used for good. An Orthodox Christian who is accustomed to praying will not eat without praying, as their conscience will not allow it. Similarly, a Christian who is used to attending church will continue to do so, as it sanctifies them. Let us build good habits that will serve our spiritual life. 

The Church is the house of salvation. A believer who is separate from the Church is like a fish out of the sea, which has no chance of survival. An Orthodox believer cannot remain in Christ if separated from the Church. The souls of living believers, those who have completed their struggle and are in heaven such as Saint George and Saint Arsema, and the holy angels, are all united by God in the Church. 

Therefore, when we go to church, we must believe that we are going to the Holy Virgin Mary, Saint Gabriel, Saint Michael, and to God Himself. King David understood this when he said in Psalm 122:1, "I rejoiced with those who said to me, 'Let us go to the house of the Lord.'"

Secondly, the Church is not just a building but the body of believers. A Christian can be the abode of Christ when they are united with the fellowship of believers, without being separated from the Church. As Jesus said in John 15:5, "I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing." Just as a branch cannot bear fruit unless it remains in the vine, a Christian cannot bear fruit unless they remain in Christ.

The third definition of the Church is the gathering of the faithful to praise God together, to listen to the Gospel, and to receive the sacraments. The holy place where these things happen is called the Church. Therefore, attending church is our Orthodox duty.

Just as we cannot live without food or shelter, the Church is our home. If we do not love the Church during our lives, we will be buried in it after death. If your husband understands and believed this, there is no reason why he would resist a church life. 

As for the question of how to raise our children, we can learn from the experience of Moses' mother. The Israelites fled from Egypt, a place where they did not know God and suffered greatly. When Moses was born, his mother placed him in the river, where Pharaoh's daughter found him and raised him. Moses' sister connected him with his mother, who raised him and taught him the right faith.

Moses chose heavenly glory over earthly rewards, and as a result, God spoke to him and used him to save Israel from the Egypt. Therefore, we should follow the example of Moses' mother and teach our children about the divinity of God, reminding them that all good things come from God.

If we raise our children in this way, it is possible to create children who say, "I want to be like Saint Kirk, like Moses, like Elias. We do not worship idols, we do not eat food offered to idols, and we deny the gods of others, for our God is the true God." It is good to teach them the word of God from a very early age.

About how our Lord and Savior #Jesus #Christ defeated the devil. 

"To destroy the works of the devil, the Son of God has been revealed" (1 John 3:8).

Dear children of God, we appreciate you very much when we see that you are following the teachings and spiritual advice that we always convey on John's Repentance page. As God has entrusted us to serve we entrust you to read and friends and family. 

Something new and wonderful happened in earth 5500 years after creation. It was a miracle that has never happened before, an abstract secret that is impossible for a creature but possible for a creator: the secret of Christ's birth from his mother, the Holy Virgin Mary, who gave Him flesh and became a man. Even though it was prophesied that He would come down from heaven and be born of Mary, it was a marvel that He was born from her body, her soul, and her flesh.

Evidence:

The apostle St. Paul wrote, "In the past God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets at many times and in various ways, but in these last days he has spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, and through whom also he made the universe" (Hebrews 1:1-2).

The apostle St. Paul said, "When the end of the age came, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law" (Galatians 4:4).

Christ's main purpose and reason for coming to earth in the flesh was to live forever in glory as the first physical word of His character. He experienced hunger, thirst, weariness, death, illness, and everything that human beings go through. This was necessary to make Him compatible with Adam's nature (1 John 3:8) so that He could destroy the works of the devil.

What is the work of the devil? The devil's work is to commit sin. Betrayal, arrogance, and falsehood are some examples of sins that the devil committed.

1st/ Betrayal

The devil, who had the position of leadership in the world of angels, arose an evil desire and sought the authority of the Creator, denying the Creatorship of God, even denying himself, and sowing the weeds of betrayal. The devil, filled with the rebellion of apostasy in his evil mind, sowed the weeds of apostasy on the hearts of Adam's children. (Mathew 13:25) But Christ removed Adam and his children from the sin of apostasy that the devil brought into the world, destroyed the tares that the devil had sown in the wheat field, and removed them from the hearts of mankind. (Ezekiel 36:25-32)

"However, false prophets were also among the people, and they will be false teachers among you, and they will deny even the Lord who redeemed them, and many will follow them in their own ways, and the path of truth will be insulted by them." (2 Peter 1:1:2) 

"For certain individuals whose condemnation was written about long ago have secretly slipped in among you. They are ungodly people, who pervert the grace of our God into a license for immorality and deny Jesus Christ our only Sovereign and Lord." (Jude 1:4) 

"He says, 'They deny religion, they are numb, as if they are burning in their own conscience'" (1 Timothy 4:2) which describes the devil's work of treason and explains his evil deeds.

(Continues) 👆

2nd / Arrogance

Pride is a behavior that originated from the devil himself. It is a devilish trait (1 Timothy 3:6). The devil, motivated by his pride, caused a division among the angels. The prophet Isaiah speaks of this pride leading to failure: "How you have fallen from heaven, morning star, son of the dawn! You have been cast down to the earth" (Isaiah 14:12).

However, our Lord has humbled us and destroyed the pride that the devil raised in our hearts. He, being the Most High God, humbled Himself and lived a sinless human life. He washed the feet of His disciples, demonstrating the wisdom that overcomes pride, which is the work of the devil (John 13:4-17). In His teachings, He exhorted us to learn from His example of meekness and lowliness of heart, assuring us that we will find rest for our souls (Matthew 11:29).

3rd / Falsehood

Falsehood is also a trait that originated from the devil himself, and he is called the father of lies (John 8:44). His aim is to twist what is good and make it evil, what is sweet and make it bitter, and to pretend that lies are truth. He misled our first parents, Adam and Eve, with his lies (Genesis 3:4-5).

But the truth of our Lord Jesus Christ has shattered the false world that the devil created (John 14:16, 1 John 2:21, John 18:37).

4th/ Homicide

When Adam and his children were first created, they didn't know about death. However, the devil was envious of them, having lost his own paradise through pride and betrayal. He wanted to cause their downfall as well, so he taught Cain to kill Abel (Gen 4).

Murder began with Cain, and all the children of Adam have lived with the stain of bloodshed. However, Christ teaches us to lay down our lives for one another and to forgive those who do evil (Luke 23:34).

Question፦ To begin, if a person is married, must they constantly attend Holy Communion with their spouse?  Because my mother really wants to partake in holy communion and has already confessed her sins when we went to Ethiopia and she did timket, but my father doesn't go to church and only follows church services from home, is it possible for my mother to take Kurban without my father or do they have to do it together because she really wants to partake in holy communion (they are married)?  

Answer፦ The question is regarding a husband and wife who are living together but are not united in their spiritual life. One of them wants to partake of Holy Communion but the other is not attending church regularly.

The first issue is that the penance fathers have not provided adequate guidance and discipline to the couple to help them walk together in their spiritual journey. This is a problem that affects many faithful believers and is a failure on the part of the penance fathers. They should show the right path and teach the way so that people can live by the teachings of the Church.  

Secondly, couples must start their marriage with a focus on their spiritual life rather than solely on material wealth and property. They should not be driven by materialistic desires, but rather by their faith. Even if they give tithes or attend church, it should not be out of obligation but rather out of love for God. It is important to seek God's kingdom and righteousness first, and all other things will be added.

Regarding the question of whether the wife can receive Holy Communion alone, the answer is no. As long as they are living together and sharing a bed, one cannot receive Holy Communion alone. If the man is not able to adjust his position and come back to the faith, and if they have exhausted all efforts to reconcile, the woman may choose to separate and receive Holy Communion alone. However, it is important to try to keep the couple together and give them advice so that they can be together until the end.

The couple should seek guidance from elders and penance fathers to avoid any unwanted issues in their relationship that may lead to separation. The father is not going to church because he lacks a Christian education but not because he hates salvation, so it is important to involve responsible fathers in this process so they can pull him into the church using the wisdom that has been given to them. 

In conclusion, it is important to prioritize one's spiritual life and seek guidance from penance fathers to walk together with one's spouse. Holy Communion entails unity in flesh and should only be received together as a couple. 

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

Question፦ What preparation is needed for repentance? What do we say when we repent?? What should we do after we repent?

Answer፦ The concept of repentance in the Orthodox Church is a fundamental question that requires careful consideration. Before embarking on the process of repentance, one must first ask oneself why they wish to repent. The reasons for repentance must be thoroughly understood, including an awareness of one's sinful nature, the need for repentance, and what one has lost by sinning. Repentance is necessary because we are all sinners, and only those who are sick need to be healed, not the healthy.

Therefore, it is important to understand the meaning of sin before repentance. Sin signifies a loss, separation, and avoidance. We lose blessings, peace, help, love, and the ability to live with God. Sin also causes deprivation and separation from holy places, prayer, blessings, and all good things.

To illustrate this point, we can examine the example of the devil, who was not initially created as an evil being. He was created as the chief of the holy angels and was close to God. However, he attempted to use his creative talents for his own benefit and was consequently cast out from the presence of God. He lost his sanctity, just as Adam was separated from God and lost his holiness, peace, and blessings. Therefore, before repenting, one must understand the severity and essence of sin and repent to regain what was lost.

When we repent, the first step is to acknowledge that we are sinners. This involves listing all of our sins, from actions to thoughts, without concealing anything. It is crucial to recognize that hiding our sins is akin to being a secret friend of the evil spirit. On the other hand, confessing our sins is living with God. We must confess to both our repentant father and to God himself. It is vital to understand that the choice to live or die is ours.

Finally, we must have the willingness to repent. Living in sin is not living. It is essential to realize that it is not right and to repent of our sinful ways. It is not challenging to turn back when we understand that the path we are on is wrong. We must hate and abhor sin and understand that it is more poisonous than poison itself. Only then can we avoid it and genuinely repent.

Moreover, repentance is a vital process that requires understanding and willingness. By acknowledging our sins, we can regain what we have lost and live with God.

(Continues)👇🏾

To summarize, it is necessary to understand the meaning of sin, acknowledge that we are sinners, confess all sins without omitting any details, and realize that we are not only confessing to the priest but also to God. Additionally, when we repent, we should not make excuses, such as blaming Satan or others. We should accept responsibility for our actions and believe that God is merciful and forgiving.

In regards to how we should confess, we should write down our sins so we don't forget anything during confession. We should not sugarcoat our sins in anyway but rather say them as they are, admitting guilt and responsibility. We should confess our sins in detail and not make superficial statements like 'I lied'. What was the lie? Why did you lie? To whom did you lie? What are the causes and effects of the lie? What are you doing to make sure this doesn't happen again? 

We can learn from the stories of those who have been forgiven, as well as follow the canons given to us by the priest. It is crucial to follow these canons precisely and accept the Holy Flesh and Precious Blood without any hindrance. After confessing and fulfilling the canons, there is nothing stopping us from receiving the Holy Body and Blood.

However, after repentance, we must stay away from sin and strive to listen to the word of God, seek advice from teachers, and sanctify ourselves. If we unintentionally fall into sin, we should rise up with repentance, and if we repeatedly fall, we must repent again and again. The journey towards God is long, and we should not separate ourselves from Him after repentance.

About St. #George 

Dear members of John's Repentance page, today is the annual feast of St. George in the EOTC and so we send you this short writing for you to learn about the life of this great saint and martyr. 

St. George is a Christian saint who is widely known for his courage, steadfast faith, and unwavering devotion to God. He was born in 280 A.D. in the city of Capadocia, which was part of the Eastern Empire in Asia Minor. He came from a wealthy and noble Christian family and followed the usual career path of young nobleman by joining the Roman army.

St. George's ability and charm quickly brought him promotion within the army, and eventually, he was made a tribune or an officer in the Imperial Guard by the Emperor. According to one story, he was a friend of Constantine, another officer who later became the first Christian emperor. The legend says that St. George accompanied Constantine to Britain and visited some holy places, including Glastonbury and Caerleon. When he returned to Nicomedia, the capital of the Eastern Empire, he encountered the fierce storm of persecution against Christians.

Diocletian, the emperor at the time, issued a formal edict against Christians on February 23, 303 A.D., which was the feast of Termhlalia. The edict mandated that all churches should be leveled to the ground, all sacred books burned, all Christians who held any honorable rank were to be degraded and deprived of civil rights, and all Christians who were not officials were to be reduced to slavery.

Despite the persecution, St. George boldly stood up for his faith. He pushed his way through the market to read the proclamation in front of the awe-stricken crowd and then deliberately tore down the Imperial edict and threw it away. This act of defiance resulted in his arrest and subsequent encounter with Diocletian.

The Emperor tried to seduce St. George by promising him a higher position in the empire, but St. George remained steadfast in his faith. Diocletian then began to threaten him with unbearable tortures that he would inflict on him. St. George refused to renounce his faith, even in the face of torture, and eventually was imprisoned.

St. George's chastity and suffering are two prominent aspects of his story. Diocletian arranged for a very beautiful woman to spend the night with him in prison to try to debauch him. St. George, who could only look forward to heavenly joy, began to pray and within a short while managed to swing her heart to the Christian faith. She seriously began to inquire about salvation, and by morning she declared that she found her true Bridegroom, Jesus Christ. With great courage, she announced her Christianity to the Emperor and his men and joined the other saintly martyrs.

(Continues)👇🏾

As for his suffering, the tortures that were applied to St. George are too numerous to mention in depth, but it is worth noting his utmost love for Christ. His body was torn by a special instrument that had metallic teeth, and our Lord Jesus rose him after his death, leading to the conversion of many pagans. He was put in active lime, and water was poured on it. Again the Lord returned him back to life. The Emperor became very agitated, imagining that the Saint was using magic. He called his top magician, Athanasius, and requested him to prepare a lethal poison to kill St. George.
The Saint signed over the cup with the sign of the cross before drinking it, and of course, no harm came to him. The Emperor's counselors informed him that St. George's magic was, in fact, contained in the sign of the Cross itself. Another cup was also given to the Saint, but this time with his hands tied behind his back. The Saint signed it by his head, saying: "shall I drink it from here or here or here or here!!!"

As St. George stood before the emperor and his court, he was given one last chance to renounce his Christian faith and offer sacrifice to the idols. The emperor promised him great rewards, honors, and privileges if he would do so. But St. George refused, declaring that he would never deny his Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

In a final act of defiance, the emperor ordered St. George to be beheaded. The saint willingly accepted his fate and went to his death with courage and grace. He is said to have uttered a prayer to God, thanking Him for the privilege of dying for the faith.

After his martyrdom, St. George's reputation as a courageous and holy man quickly spread throughout the Christian world. Churches were built in his honor, and his feast day was celebrated on this April 23rd. He became known as the patron saint of soldiers, knights, and all who defend the faith.

Today, the legend of St. George and the dragon is still celebrated in many cultures around the world. It has become a symbol of strength, courage, and the triumph of good over evil. The story of St. George reminds us that even in the face of persecution and adversity, we can remain steadfast in our faith and trust in God's love and mercy.
