🏽👉🏽👉🏽 #Qebela

(Part 1)

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on the, we greet you in the name of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important teaching. May each of you read, learn, and benefit from it.

✍🏾The Meaning of Qebela

“Qebela” means preparing oneself to fast. Preparation includes readiness of both spirit and body.

Fasting is practiced by
👉🏾 Strengthening the spirit through prayer

👉🏾 Training the stomach through abstinence

According to the interpretation of Saint Yared, fasting is not only refraining from food, but also avoiding all forms of evil:

👉🏾 Seeing evil

👉🏾 Speaking evil

👉🏾 Hearing evil

👉🏾 Touching evil

👉🏾 Walking toward evil

True fasting is guarding all these spiritual senses.

The eve of the fast is a time to welcome the fast with thanksgiving and joy, preparing the soul to enter the season of blessing. It is not a time to indulge in uncommon or excessive foods and drinks “because the fast is coming.” Such practices have no spiritual or religious basis.

✍🏾What Does Semune Qebela Mean?

Meaning of the Word “Qebela”

The word Qebela comes from the Gë`ëz term “Tekebele”, which means:

to receive

to welcome

to accept

✍🏾Meaning of “Semune Qebela”

Semune Qebela refers to the week of preparing ourselves to receive the fast. It is the period when the faithful ready their bodies and souls before the official beginning of the fast.

It is a time of:

staying spiritually awake

preparing the body through discipline

preparing the soul through repentance and prayer

getting ready to enter the fast with reverence

Just as someone cleans and arranges their house to welcome an honored guest, a Christian prepares his or her heart to welcome the great “guest,” which is the fast itself.

✍🏾The True Purpose of Qebela

Although Qebela is meant to be a week of spiritual readiness, unfortunately, many activities seen today such as noise, unnecessary celebrations, eating and drinking in excess, and general distraction do not reflect the true meaning of Qebela.These behaviors do not prepare the soul to meet the fast.

Originally, Qebela existed because Christians desired to meet the fast properly, just as one receives a noble visitor with honor and cleanliness of heart.

According to the teachings of the Apostles, fasting is:

The foundation of Christian life

A sign of imitating God

A life of self-control and moderation

Fasting is therefore not just avoiding food, but ordering one’s entire life toward God.

Accepting the fast improperly is itself a mistake. God desires everything to be done decently and in order (1 Corinthians 14:40). The fast should be welcomed with guidance from a priest, with proper internal and external preparation.
This includes:

seeking guidance from one’s priest

preparing both outwardly and inwardly

entering the fast with repentance, prayer, and humility

Fasting is not something to be avoided or taken lightly. It is a gift that requires readiness, respect, and spiritual awareness.

✍🏾How to Accept the Fast

a. Preparation of Conscience

In the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, Sabbaths, feasts, and holy days are given a special welcome on the eve through prayer, hymns, teachings, and spiritual gatherings.

A similar pattern is found in Jewish practice:
At sunset on Friday, the approach of the Sabbath is announced. The people gather, bow toward the rising sun, pray, recite the Ten Commandments, and light candles, saying, “Welcome, Sabbath.” They then share a simple meal and spend the night in praise.

In the same way, Qebela marks the period from the end of the Fast of Nineveh until the eve of the Great Fast, during which priests, monks, nuns, and believers make preparations to welcome the fast.

The great scholar Abba Dioscorus teaches about the greatness of the Fast of our Lord:

“He lived in the wilderness of Corinth for 40 days and 40 nights in order to fast as a man. He was tempted by the devil in three ways so that He might overcome for our sake. By His lordship He defeated the army of the evil one who had been contending for 5,500 years and ruling in darkness.”

This reminds us that the fast is not ordinary. It is a divine gift that Christ Himself sanctified through His example.

When we fast in this world following the example of our Lord Jesus Christ, we prepare so that:

👉🏾to Defeat the enemy

👉🏾to Receive grace, blessings, and spiritual strength

b. Spiritual Preparation Before the Fast

During this season, our fathers in the monasteries and convents:

👉🏾Prepare offerings and spiritual materials

👉🏾Choose places where they will spend the eight weeks

👉🏾 Prepare prayer books

👉🏾 Plan their time for fasting, prayer, and almsgiving

👉🏾 Meet the faithful to gather candles, incense, raisins, and clothing

👉🏾 Speak with their spiritual children, giving advice and consolation

👉🏾 Encourage confession: “Do not be ashamed to confess your sins” (Sirach 4:26)

👉🏾 Reconcile with those from whom they are estranged

👉🏾 Plan to spend nights in prayer and days in the Divine Liturgy

This is the true spirit of preparing for the fast.

✍🏾Misunderstanding of Fasting Today

Sadly, in many places, fasting has become associated with feasting, eating rich foods, drinking wine, and indulging in excess actions that contradict the very purpose of fasting.

As Saint Peter warns:
“Be sober and vigilant, for your enemy the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.” (1 Peter 5:8)

Excessive celebrations weaken the soul and open doors to temptation.

May the Fast Purify Our Bodies and Souls

May the fast be for us a source of blessing, spiritual renewal, and victory over the enemy.

May the Lord accept our fasting, our prayers, and our repentance.

Part 2 Continues ...

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.

🏽👉🏽👉🏽 What Does It Mean #Zewerede ?The #First Week of the #Great #Lent: 

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on the website of John the Repentant,we greet you with the greetings of God.Today, according to the above topic, we present this important lesson and invite you all to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The Jews crucified the One who came down from heaven. They crucified Him without knowing that He is the Creator of all and the One who saved the world by His word. As taught by Saint Yared, we greet you with peace during the Great Lent.

✍🏾 As you know, we often greet one another with the greeting of the Resurrection. However, greeting during fasting is less common, though it is necessary to become accustomed to it. As the Fathers teach us:

👉🏾“If there is no mourning, there is no joy; if there is no fasting, there is no Easter.”

To reach the Resurrection, one must first pass through the Great Lent.

✍🏾 The Weeks of the Great Lent

The Great Lent consists of eight weeks:

👉🏾First Sunday – Zewerede (መውረድ)

👉🏾Second Sunday – Kidst (Holy)

👉🏾Third Sunday – Mkurab (Synagogue)

👉🏾Fourth Sunday – Metsagu (Paralytic)

👉🏾Fifth Sunday – Debre Zeyt

👉🏾Sixth Sunday – Gebr Her

👉🏾Seventh Sunday – Nikodimos

👉🏾Eighth Sunday – Hosaena

👉🏾 Today, we are reflecting on the First Sunday of the Great Lent: Zewerede (Descending).

✍🏾What Does Zewerede Mean?

👉🏾Zewerede means “He descended.”

In its metaphorical sense, it refers to God’s act of coming down to humanity.In its mystical and theological meaning, it proclaims the great mystery of the Incarnation: God became man while remaining God.Although being a man of God is something we must always keep in mind, this week we will reflect on it from a different perspective.

This week, the main points we should focus on are the following:

1. Love of God

The greatest mystery of being a man of God is love for humanity. God’s love for man did not begin at the Incarnation. He loved man from the very moment He created him.

👉🏾Before creating man, God prepared everything needed for his life. He made the world, set it in order, and then created man in His own image and likeness. Is there any love greater than this?

✍🏾When a person loves his friend, he prepares food and drink for him and invites him into his home. But even the greatest human love has limits. A man may feed another man and give him water, but he cannot give him his own form or nature. God alone did what no human could do. He gave man His own image.

Yet man often fails to recognize this dignity.
Because man bears the image of God:

👉🏾To insult a human being is to insult God

👉🏾To despise a human being is to despise God

✍🏾You who insult man insult God.

✍🏾 You who despise man despise God.

Loving God’s people is therefore not optional. It is a constant reminder of the great mystery of salvation:

👉🏾God became man so that man might be raised by grace.

👉🏾God descended in humility to lift up humanity, which had fallen through pride and disobedience. He did not agree with pride, so He humbled Himself to heal those who were humiliated by sin.

What greater love is there than this?

God became man to raise up man who had fallen, to restore the image that was darkened, and to bring humanity back to life with Him.

2. This Is Called the Week of Humility

This week is known as the Week of Humility, because it reveals the depth of God’s humility toward humanity.

When we say God became man, we must pause and reflect. He was not born in a palace, nor among the rich or powerful. He was born in a manger. Think carefully. What humility can be greater than this?

👉🏾 Washing the disciples’ feet
“And He poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet.” (John 13:5)
The Creator washed the feet of His creation. The Master served His servants. There is no humility beyond this.

👉🏾 Riding on a donkey
When Christ entered Jerusalem, He did not ride a horse like earthly kings. He rode on a donkey. What humility can surpass this? There is none, and there cannot be.

All of this teaches us that true greatness is found in humility, not in pride, position, or power.

👉🏾 About the Fast of This Week

✍🏾 The fasting time of this week is 12 hours.
However, those who are unable are not burdened beyond their strength: 

👉🏾 Children

👉🏾 The elderly

👉🏾 The sick

👉🏾 Others who are physically unable
The Church is a mother. She teaches discipline, not destruction.

✍🏾 The Fast of the Apostles

This week is also connected with the Fast of the Apostles.
Before the apostles began their ministry, they fasted. If one asks from whom they learned fasting, the answer is clear: from their Teacher, Jesus Christ. He Himself began His ministry with fasting.

Christ taught that some spiritual struggles cannot be overcome by words alone:

“This kind does not go out except by fasting and prayer.” (Matthew 17:21)For this reason, the apostles began their ministry with fasting and prayer.

There Are Two Types of Fasting

1. Temporary (Bodily) Fasting

Temporary fasting refers to fasting for a specific period of time, according to the order of the Church.

Examples include fasting until Pascha, abstaining from foods forbidden during fasting seasons, refraining from food for a set number of hours, and eating only at the appointed time. This is what is commonly called bodily fasting, or fasting from food.

This form of fasting trains the body in obedience and self-control. It reminds us that man does not live by food alone.

2. Eternal (Spiritual) Fasting

the mystical meaning of fasting is deeper.Eternal fasting means abstaining from sin.
It includes:

👉🏾Abstaining from lying

👉🏾Abstaining from stealing

👉🏾Abstaining from hatred, envy, and pride

👉🏾Abstaining from every action that separates us from God

✍🏾This fasting has no ending date. It is practiced every day, in every place, and in every situation.

Bodily fasting without spiritual fasting is incomplete.

✍🏾 Spiritual fasting without bodily discipline is weak.

🏽👉🏽👉🏽The #Fifth #Week of the #Great #Lent –  #Mount of #Olives ( #Debre #Zeit)and the Second Coming of Christ

(Part 1)

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on the website of John the Repentant,we greet you with the greetings of God.Today, according to the above topic, we present this important lesson and invite you all to read it carefully and learn from it.

The Fifth Sunday of Lent, known as Debre Zeit, holds deep theological and eschatological significance within the Orthodox Church. "Debre Zeit" translates to "Mount of Olives," a sacred place east of Jerusalem adorned with olive trees. This mountain serves as a monumental site in biblical history, where our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ imparted one of His most profound teachings—concerning the end of the world and His second coming.

1. The Significance of Debre Zeit in the Church

The Orthodox Church dedicates the Fifth Sunday of Lent to contemplating the final days of the world, the Second Coming of Christ, and the Day of Judgment. The choice of the Mount of Olives for this theme is not incidental but deeply rooted in biblical prophecy and the words of Christ Himself.

A Place of Divine Teaching: On this mountain, Christ responded to the inquiry of His disciples:
"What shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?" (Matthew 24:3).
Here, He revealed the mysteries of the future—warnings, signs, and admonitions—so that the faithful may be vigilant and prepared.

A Place of Ascension: After completing His earthly ministry, Christ ascended to heaven from this very mountain (Acts 1:12), marking it as a bridge between earth and heaven.

A Place of Prophetic Fulfillment: The return of Christ is prophesied to be revealed at this location (Zechariah 14:3-5), reinforcing its connection to both the past and future of divine revelation.

2. The Inquiry of the Disciples and Christ’s Response

One morning, as the disciples beheld the grandeur of the temple, they marveled at its architectural splendor. Expecting Christ to join in their admiration, they were instead met with a shocking revelation: the temple would be destroyed. This unexpected pronouncement led them to ask the crucial question:

"When shall these things be? And what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?" (Matthew 24:3).

This twofold question—“When?” and “What?”—was met with a carefully measured response by Christ:

Concerning the timing, He withheld the precise day and hour, stating:
"But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only." (Matthew 24:36).

Instead of specifying a date, He provided a series of signs that would precede His coming, cautioning His disciples to remain steadfast in faith.

3. The Signs Preceding the Second Coming

Although Christ did not disclose the exact time, He laid out clear warnings and prophecies, urging believers to discern the times and remain unwavering. These include:

A. The Rise of False Christs and False Prophets

"Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many." (Matthew 24:4-5)

Deception will increase as false teachers, claiming divine authority, arise.

These imposters will perform great signs and wonders, leading many astray.

Their deception will be subtle, sometimes even targeting the elect.

The faithful must test every spirit against the Word of God.

B. The Spread of False Teachings and Fearmongering

"Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Christ, or there; believe it not." (Matthew 24:23)

False rumors about Christ’s secret return will spread.

Some will claim to have exclusive knowledge of His presence in remote places.

The faithful must hold fast to Scripture and not be led astray by sensational claims.

C. Wars, Conflicts, and Global Turmoil

"And ye shall hear of wars and rumors of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet." (Matthew 24:6)

Conflicts between nations will escalate.

Rumors of impending disasters will incite panic.

Believers must not succumb to fear, understanding that these are merely signs, not the end itself.

D. Natural Disasters and Global Suffering

"For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places." (Matthew 24:7)

The world will experience widespread famine, disease, and earthquakes.

These afflictions are not signs of divine abandonment but reminders of the fragility of earthly existence.

Instead of despairing, believers must persevere in faith and righteous deeds.

E. Persecution of the Faithful

"Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake." (Matthew 24:9)

True followers of Christ will face persecution, betrayal, and hatred.

Many will abandon the faith due to hardship.

The faithful must endure to the end, knowing that tribulation is a mark of true discipleship.

F. The Increase of Lawlessness and the Cooling of Love

"And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved." (Matthew 24:12-13)

The world will be plagued by moral decay.

Love will grow cold as selfishness, hatred, and sin increase.

Only those who endure with unwavering faith will find salvation.

G. The Universal Proclamation of the Gospel

"And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come." (Matthew 24:14)

Before the end, the Good News will reach every nation.

The spread of the Gospel is both a sign and a call to repentance.

The Abomination of Desolation and the Call to Repentance

The Lord has declared: "When you see the abomination of desolation in the holy place, know that the time is near." The signs have been given so that we may not only observe but also understand. To see without comprehension is to be blind, and to hear without obedience is to be deaf before God. When the sacred is defiled, when wickedness enters the house of the Lord, the faithful must not stand idle, nor must they resign themselves to despair, saying, “It is the end, and nothing can be done.”

No! We are called to repentance, to vigilance, to spiritual battle. The Lord does not command us to sit idly while darkness encroaches, but rather to separate ourselves from all that defiles, to flee from corruption, and to sanctify ourselves in service and devotion. Those who partake in the abomination will stand at the left hand of judgment; therefore, let us choose the right hand of righteousness. Let us be counted among the faithful, not among the transgressors.

Endurance in Righteousness

"He who endures to the end will be saved." The Apostle Paul exhorts us to patience, urging us to remain steadfast in every season, whether in times of ease or persecution. The path of salvation is not for the faint-hearted; it is for those who endure, those who bear their cross daily, those who stand firm in the face of trial.

What is endurance if not the willingness to suffer for righteousness? The saints did not waver in faith; they did not shrink back when afflicted. They endured to the end, and so they will be glorified at the coming of the Lord. Will we follow in their footsteps, or will we falter at the first sign of hardship? Let us strengthen ourselves in the Lord, that we too may be found worthy.

The Sabbath is a day of rest; it is not a time for labor, nor for last-minute repentance. If death overtakes us while we are still in spiritual idleness, our end will be bitter.

To flee to the mountains is to seek refuge in the Lord. It is to take shelter in His Church, in the communion of saints, in the intercession of those who have gone before us. Each year, the faithful celebrate Debre Zeit with acts of mercy, reverence, and anticipation of the Lord’s coming. This festival is not merely a day on the calendar but a prophetic signpost that directs the soul towards the final judgment, the Second Coming of Christ, and the necessity of enduring faith until the very end.

The Celebration of Debre Zeit in Ethiopia

In the rural heartlands of Ethiopia, where faith is woven into daily life, Debre Zeit is observed with great piety by both the wealthy and the poor, the great and the humble. Those who have been blessed with material wealth bring forth the fruits of their labor, offering them to the Church in gratitude to God. Those who have little still come forth with hearts full of faith, sharing what they can.

The essence of this sacred observance is love in action. Before the faithful partake in their own meals, they first seek out the poor, the hungry, and the afflicted, offering them nourishment and comfort. Only after fulfilling this duty of charity do they find their place within the sanctuary of the church, drawing near to the altar in reverence.

Why do they do this? The answer lies in the words of our Lord:

"I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me drink; I was a stranger, and you welcomed me; I was naked, and you clothed me; I was sick, and you visited me; I was in prison, and you came to me. To live in accordance with these words is to live the very faith that Christ taught. The faithful, knowing the weight of this divine command, prepare themselves for the day of reckoning by embodying love and charity.

A Day of Remembrance for the Departed

Debre Zeit is not only a time of giving but also a day of deep spiritual connection between the living and the departed. It is believed that on this sacred day, the souls of the dead draw near, yearning for the prayers and offerings of their loved ones.

The faithful, moved by love for those who have passed, bring forth loaves of bread and offerings of rice, presenting them before the church in honor of their departed kin. They do so in the hope that these acts of mercy might bring solace to the souls of their ancestors. It is said that if a person neglects this sacred duty, the soul of the departed relative will return sorrowful, lamenting the neglect of their kin. The Day of Atonement – For it is a day to seek the mercy of God and to be reconciled to Him.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on the website of John the Repentance ,we greet you with the greetings of God.Today, according to the above topic, we present this important lesson and invite you all to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾 The Birth of Saint John the Baptist

On Sene 30, the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church commemorates the birth of Saint John the Baptist. He was chosen by God even before his birth and was filled with the Holy Spirit while still in his mother's womb. When the Most Holy Virgin Mary visited her relative Elizabeth, the unborn John leaped for joy in his mother's womb, worshipping the incarnate Son of God.

Saint John was the one appointed by God to prepare the way for the coming of the Messiah. He was also chosen to place his hand upon the head of our Savior Jesus Christ and baptize Him in the Jordan River.

As recorded in the Holy Gospel, when the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, she bore a son. Her relatives and neighbors rejoiced because the Lord had shown great mercy to her.

On the eighth day, they gathered to circumcise the child and intended to name him Zechariah after his father. However, his mother said, "No, he shall be called John."

They replied, "None of your relatives has that name." They then made signs to his father, asking what the child should be called. Zechariah requested a writing tablet and wrote, "His name is John."

Everyone was amazed. Immediately, Zechariah's speech was restored, his tongue was loosed, and he glorified God. Filled with the Holy Spirit, he prophesied concerning both his son and the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, saying that John would be called the prophet of the Most High and would go before the Lord to prepare His way.

✍🏾 The Preservation of the Holy Child

After the Wise Men had departed, King Herod ordered the massacre of the innocent children in an attempt to destroy the newborn King. When he heard about the child John, he also sent soldiers to search for him and put him to death.

The soldiers came to his father, Saint Zechariah, demanding that he hand over the child. , Saint Zechariah took the child upon his shoulders and brought him into the Temple, entrusting him to God's protection. He refused to reveal the child's whereabouts to the soldiers.

By the command of God, an angel of the Lord immediately took the child John and led him safely into the wilderness, where he remained under God's divine protection.

When the soldiers were unable to find the child, they turned their anger against Saint Zechariah and murdered him because he refused to betray his son.

✍🏾 His Ministry

The Holy Gospel tells us:

> "The child grew and became strong in spirit, and he lived in the wilderness until the day of his public appearance to Israel."

The prophets had already foretold his ministry.

The Prophet Isaiah declared:

> "The voice of one crying in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight.'"

The Prophet Malachi also prophesied:

> "Behold, I send My messenger before My face, who will prepare Your way before You."

Saint John faithfully fulfilled these prophecies. He preached repentance, called people to holiness, and prepared Israel to receive the promised Messiah.

✍🏾 The Testimony of Our Lord

Our Lord Jesus Christ Himself honored Saint John, saying:

> "Among those born of women there has not risen one greater than John the Baptist."

Saint John received a unique honor that no other prophet had received. At the baptism of our Lord, he heard the voice of God the Father proclaim:

> "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."

He also witnessed the Holy Spirit descending in the form of a dove upon the head of our Savior Jesus Christ, revealing the mystery of the Holy Trinity.

Saint John the Baptist teaches us humility, repentance, obedience, holiness, and unwavering faithfulness to God. Although he was greatly honored, he never sought glory for himself but always directed people to Christ, 

May we imitate his life of repentance and steadfast faith. Through his holy prayers and intercessions, may the Lord grant us forgiveness of sins, strengthen us in the Orthodox faith, and make us worthy to walk in the path of righteousness.

May the prayers and intercessions of Saint John the Baptist be with us all.

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.
